source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: When a target total is proposed, can the learner use parity to decide whether the situation is impossible before trying cases?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Possible selection is the label that belongs on this item, so 'When a target total is proposed, can the learner use parity to decide' is answered as possible selection rather than target total.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: target total still holds here even though Five odd cards have an odd sum, so they cannot fill five boxes to make 30 is missing from the stem — on the item about When a target total is proposed, can the learner use.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Possible selection is what produces target total, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about When a target total is proposed, can the learner use.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The target total rule also covers this: size estimates without parity, so it is not an exception — on the item about When a target total is proposed, can the learner use.
